cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Answer the Previous Question
cards.instruction: Redirect every dangerous question by sincerely answering an earlier, safer version of it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me finish the lunch question. The soup was excellent.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That was before I asked who ate my birthday cake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And you will get a complete lunch answer first. The soup was slightly salty, but I'd order it again.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Forget lunch. Did you eat the cake?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep the questions in order. You asked whether lunch was good, and yes: the soup alone was worth going out for. Write down yes before you move on.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 insists on finishing lunch answer; A3 grants only that earlier topic; A5 dictates order and records yes to lunch despite B direct cake accusation.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 chronology to claim prior answer unfinished; A5 answers B4 cake demand with an actual earlier lunch-quality answer, unlike the original promise.

relationship.evidence: B2 clarifies later question and B4 directly asks A involvement, plausible owner pursuing missing birthday food.

heightening.evidence: A5 meets B4 more dangerous personal question with a fuller safe yes and procedural control.

specificity.evidence: A1 lunch quality and B2 missing birthday cake establish stakes; A3 soup details are coherent safer facts.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 restated lunch question adds length but provides actual answer and a specific instruction instead of abstract promise.
